newsitem.title: GERMANY: Union seeks wage rise in Lufthansa talks.
newsitem.headline: Union seeks wage rise in Lufthansa talks.

text.p: Germany's OeTV union said on Thursday it would be seeking wage rises and guarantees on job protection when negotiations start with airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG on Monday.

"Job security is the central demand of the OeTV in this year's wage round with Lufthansa," the public sector and transport union said in a statement, adding that it would also be seeking a 12-month wage pact based on a 2.3 percent rise.

Lufthansa earlier this week said it would be calling for a wage freeze that could last for up to three years but said it was ready to discuss employment guarantees and a plan to offer employees bonuses related to the performance of the business.
The wage freeze has already been rejected by the white collar union DAG, the other union who will be involved in talks with Lufthansa.
OeTV said it wanted to secure a "rationalisation protection" agreement which would be valid even if the airline lost market share or closed routes.
The union said it would also be calling on the Lufthansa board to keep what it called a promise to receive a share of some of the group's 1995 profits.
